title: Drift, then a test: is the simulation consistent with Kimura?
intro: Two engines in a chain. First 200 populations of N diploid individuals drift for 400 generations (Wright–Fisher), and we count in how many of them allele A is fixed. Then probability theory judges the count: an exact binomial test asks whether it fits Kimura’s fixation probability, and a 95% Wilson interval shows which fixation probabilities the count allows. Change N, the starting frequency and the selection coefficient.
sLabel: Selection coefficient s (AA 1 + s, Aa 1 + s/2)
ciLoLabel: 95% interval for the fixation probability: from
ciHiLabel: 95% interval for the fixation probability: to

insideLabel: Kimura’s value lies inside the interval
